## 1. Continuous Batching (Dynamic / Paged Batching)

### Concept & Mechanism
Traditional static batching groups incoming inference requests into fixed-size batches (e.g., $B = 32$) at the moment of arrival. If only 4 requests arrive in 100 ms, the server idles for the remainder of the batch cycle, wasting compute (latency penalty) and memory bandwidth. Conversely, if a sudden burst pushes requests beyond capacity, requests queue excessively or get dropped.

**Continuous batching** decouples batch formation from token generation. Instead of locking a batch for the entire sequence generation, the server dynamically:

# Technical Deep Dive: LLM Inference Server Architecture

Modern Large Language Model (LLM) inference differs fundamentally from standard software execution. Because autoregressive models generate text token-by-token, naive serving architectures quickly encounter severe compute, memory, and latency bottlenecks. High-performance inference engines (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang) rely on a suite of coordinated systems: **Continuous Batching**, **Key-Value (KV) Caches**, **Prefix Reuse**, **Speculative Decoding**, and careful balancing of **Latency vs. Throughput**.
